relations.subject: Shi Yuanying
relations.evidence: he received ordination as a monk at Meifeng Temple in Fuzhou under master Zeng Xi (增西上人)

relations.subject: Shi Yuanying
relations.evidence: received prātimokṣa under master Miao Lian (妙蓮老和尚) at Yongquan Temple.

relations.subject: Shi Yuanying
relations.evidence: When he was 21, he began to learn Chan Buddhism under master Ye Kai (冶開老和尚), he stayed with his teacher for four years.

relations.subject: Shi Yuanying
relations.evidence: At the age of 25, he resided in Tiantong Temple with his teacher Bazhi Toutuo (八指頭陀).

relations.subject: Shi Yuanying
relations.evidence: In 1909, he became the abbot of Jiedai Temple.

relations.subject: Shi Yuanying
relations.evidence: In 1912, the Chinese Buddhist Association was founded and he was elected a councilor.

relations.subject: Shi Yuanying
relations.evidence: In 1917, Yuanying was elected Venerable Master of the Buddhist Association of Ningbo

relations.subject: Shi Yuanying
relations.evidence: In 1929, along with Taixu and others, Yuanying formed the China Buddhist Association in Shanghai, where he was president.

relations.subject: Shi Yuanying
relations.evidence: In 1929, along with Taixu and others, Yuanying formed the China Buddhist Association in Shanghai, where he was president.

relations.subject: Shi Yuanying
relations.evidence: In 1930, Yuanying became the abbot of Tiantong Temple, where he taught Chan Buddhism for six years.

relations.subject: Shi Yuanying
relations.evidence: In 1937, he was the abbot of Yongquan Temple, at the age of 60.

relations.subject: Shi Yuanying

relations.evidence: In 1945, he founded the Yuanming Lengyan School (圓明楞嚴專宗學院), where he served as president
